messages:
Irene: Quick follow-up from the sync: we need to lock down the anchor grammar before we publish the RFC. Current proposal uses mixed separators (slash and =). That causes subtle parsing differences in routing libs.
Leo: Agreed. Suggestion: formal grammar -> <kind> '/' <identifier> OR <kind> ':' <kv-list>. Examples: tenant/alpha, canary:cohort=42;reason=smoke. Keeps simple cases short, allows metadata when needed.
Mayank: I like the two-form approach. A couple of edge cases: identifiers can contain hyphens and dots, but we should forbid '/' inside identifiers to keep parsing trivial. Also max length? Recommend 128 chars.
Clara: Validation rules we should enforce at ingress: regex for kind (ascii letters, hyphen), identifier allowed chars, and kv-list parsed by splitting on ',' where each pair is key=value (no nested commas). We'll add a strict schema in jsonschema for services.
Irene: Good. Also propose a small controlled vocabulary for kind: tenant, stable, pinned, canary, ephemeral. Anything else becomes meta_tags. That avoids freeform proliferation.
Leo: For meta info (stability_score, deprecation_hint) we keep them as top-level optional fields. But we should distinguish routing-critical data (anchor) from telemetry-only fields. Routers should only trust anchor and controlled tags.
Mayank: On resolver behavior: define deterministic priority when multiple inputs exist (anchor, legacy pin_type, tenant_scope). I propose resolver chooses in this order: explicit anchor > tenant_scope > pin_type > fallback. When mapping legacy -> anchor, add resolver_hint header so services know source.
Clara: We'll standardize the header as X-Anchor-Resolved: <schema-v>, plus X-Anchor-Source: anchor|tenant_scope|pin_type. Also include X-Anchor-Hash for deduped caching.
pin-resolver-bot: FYI dry-run results: transformed 12 services in staging. 3 services emitted ambiguous anchors (two legacy fields present and conflicting). Logs: "ambig:svc=flux,legacy_pin=staging,tenant_scope=tenantA". PRs created for fixes.
Irene: Ambiguity handling: resolver should detect conflict and prefer the highest-priority source but emit a high-severity telemetry event. We should also surface conflicts to the Console with a link to the offending object.
Leo: Telemetry event schema idea: event_type="anchor_resolution", fields: resolver_version, chosen_anchor, primary_source, conflicting_sources[], raw_legacy_fields. Keep payload small.
Mayank: Also recommend a periodic job that scans sstable for objects using legacy fields and reports mismatch rates per service. This will guide removal schedule.
Clara: About migration timeline: propose opt-in deprecation window: 30 days of telemetry collection -> 90-day remediation -> 30-day final warning -> removal. For critical infra we can have extended windows.
Irene: Library support: we'll publish a tiny language-agnostic resolver spec and provide official clients in go/python/node that return a small struct: {anchor, sources, header_values}. Keep API minimal.
Leo: Security note: anchor values may leak tenant IDs in logs; we need a redaction policy before writing raw anchors to low-priv logs. Use hashed forms for telemetry where possible.
Mayank: Good call. For telemetry keep both hashed_anchor and plain_kind only. Only Console admin logs show full anchor with RBAC.
Clara: Router compatibility: implement a conservative parser at first that only accepts exact grammar. We'll add incremental parsing extensions behind feature flags.
Irene: Final: I'll update the draft RFC with grammar BNF, jsonschema examples, header definitions, telemetry event spec, migration timeline, and client lib APIs. Target to post tomorrow for review. :white_check_mark:
